title: EMU Admission Note - Epilepsy Surgery Evaluation

FICTIONAL NOTE WRITTEN FOR A PORTFOLIO DEMO. NOT A REAL PATIENT.

Assessment and Plan
Principal Problem: Localization-related (focal) epilepsy with impaired awareness seizures, intractable
Alex Rivera is a 29 y.o. left handed male admitted to the EMU for epilepsy surgery evaluation.
His seizures have not been controlled on two adequate anti-seizure medication trials, so his epilepsy is considered medically refractory.
- Admit to EMU and initiate continuous video-EEG monitoring to localize seizure onset.
- Anti-seizure medications: taper levetiracetam by 50% tonight. Continue lacosamide 200mg twice daily.
Rescue Plan: lorazepam 2mg IV PRN for seizures longer than 3 minutes.

HPI
Mr. Rivera works full time as a warehouse supervisor. He is not currently driving because of his seizures.
Seizure Onset Age: 17
Seizure type 1: focal impaired awareness seizures. Rising epigastric sensation, then staring, lip smacking, and unresponsiveness for about 60 seconds, followed by confusion.
Seizure Frequency: weekly, often in clusters of 2 to 3 events over one day.
Previous Anti-seizure Drugs tried: lamotrigine (rash).
Home medications: levetiracetam 1500mg twice daily, lacosamide 200mg twice daily. He reports irritability on levetiracetam.
No history of prior epilepsy surgery, VNS, or RNS.
No history of suicidal ideation.

Past Medical History: Anxiety. Migraine headaches.
Past Surgical History: Appendectomy (2015).

Previous workup:
MRI brain (1/2026): left mesial temporal sclerosis with left hippocampal atrophy. Otherwise normal.
FDG-PET: not yet performed, ordered for this admission.
fMRI and WADA: not performed.
